cost: THE TARGET IS NOT REACHED AND THE ROUND SAYS SO. 92 +-2 was asked for; 95 is what the board gives with every pin held. Doctrine 1: the closest reachable value is landed and the rest is declined with the frontier below, rather than reached by a per-team override.

THE FRONTIER, measured on the whole 1,255-five wheel (scripts/diag-team/front133.py, 9,000 sampled points over the four channel weights, ANCHOR_SOFT, ANCHOR_2ND, the load profile and the glass shape, every point graded against all fifteen DEF pins and the 47-season within-season Spearman): with the fit held at or above shipped the subject's floor is 95. 94 costs rho +0.7764 -> +0.7712 and six simultaneous knobs. 93 costs +0.7657. 92 costs +0.7544 (-0.022) and a full seven-knob refit of the didx. There is no single-knob path to 92.

THE PIN THAT BINDS IS THE WARRIORS '17 (recal_122, 81 +-5, reading 76 — ON its floor, unrounded 75.55). The subject is a top-heavy five (perdef 93/90/69/68/59) and so are the Warriors (96/71/66/62/45), and the subject beats them at EVERY slot except the best defender. So no monotone re-reading of the five's perdef can lower one without lowering the other: the required ratio is 33:1 in relative didx loss and the best channel ratio available is 3.7:1. That is the whole reason 92 is out of reach, and it is a conflict between two of his own rulings, not a modelling gap.

DIDX_HOLD is re-derived, not re-tuned: 1.0773 -> 0.4523, chosen so the pool's mean drtgRef is 110.047736 before and after, to six decimal places. The DEF gauge block in src/engine/gauges.ts (DEF_WORST/DEF_MID/DEF_TOP + the 47-season DEF_LEVEL table) is FROZEN by recal_108 and was NOT re-derived.

DKNOBS.ANCHOR_2ND (0.35) — the standalone `teamDefense` path — is deliberately UNTOUCHED, on recal_94's precedent for DISC_FREEPTS: it is a different layer, off the gauge path and off the resolver's path, read only by tests/offense.test.ts.

MEASURED AND NOT TAKEN, written down so a later round does not re-measure it: the GLASS channel's shape is wrong too. `glass` reads the five's defensive board as d0 + 0.5*d1 + 0.1*(d2+d3+d4) — the top two men take 83% of the credit, the pre-recal_122 top-heavy stack. Against the channel's own truth column (bref drb_percent, within-season Spearman over the same 1,255) the shipped stack scores +0.3124 and [1, .5, .35, .35, .35] scores +0.3476. Fixing it is right, but it is worth ~0 on the subject once the channel's spread is held, and it costs the whole-dial rho ~0.004 — so it is not this round's lever and it is not smuggled in. Its own round should take it, with the opponent side (o0 + 0.5*o1 + 0.25*rest) checked against orb_percent at the same time.

The campaign ladder was regenerated (npm run opponents). The League tier — src/data/opponents.json, all 30 levels — is bit-identical in order and in every five. notes: THE MEASUREMENT. Truth is data/bref/Team Summaries.csv; the instrument is the within-season Spearman of the shipped dial against real DRtg over the 1,255 fieldable team-seasons of src/data/teamseasons.json, averaged over 47 seasons — the same instrument rounds 94, 100, 110 and 122 used. The whole round is scripts/diag-team: lab133.py (the bench: recomputes every five's didx/drtgRef/dial under a parametrised didx, re-holds the pool mean and grades all fifteen pins), scan133*.py (one knob family at a time), reg133.py + drb133.py + four133.py (the channels against their OWN truth columns), opt133.py / front133.py / grid133.py (the frontier), final133.py + fine133.py (the landing), parity133.ts (py/ts on the subject five), ten133.ts (the ten teams through the app's own seasonGauges).

THE SUBJECT, TERM BY TERM, BEFORE. 76ers '85 perdef 93 (Cheeks) / 90 (Bobby Jones) / 69 (Erving) / 68 (Barkley) / 59 (Moses), rimprot 90 and 88. didx 67.277 = 0.55 x effDi 77.60 (42.680) + anchor 12.658 + steals 4.805 + glass 8.211 - hold 1.077. drtgRef 107.778, DEF 96, all-time #11, 2nd of the 22 fieldable 1985 fives. Real DRtg 107.3 — 10th of 22, with a league-average shot defence. The anchor line is the tell: anchorRaw = 90 + 0.35 x 88 x 88/99 = 117.38, so Bobby Jones standing next to Moses Malone was worth +27.4 raw rim points, more than a quarter of the whole channel, off a scale whose top is 99.

WHAT WAS NEVER TESTED. ANCHOR_2ND has been 0.35 since the first defence build; recal_94 capped the anchor, recal_122 turned the cap into a knee, and neither ever asked what the second rim protector is actually worth. bref carries the channel's own truth column — the rim anchor exists to hold the opponent's SHOOTING down, so its outcome is opp_e_fg_percent — and the within-season Spearman of anchorRaw against it over the same 1,255 team-seasons is a clean single-peaked curve: 0.00 +0.5086 · 0.10 +0.5228 · 0.15 +0.5289 · 0.20 +0.5275 · 0.25 +0.5240 · 0.30 +0.5246 · 0.35 +0.5180 (shipped) · 0.45 +0.5087 · 0.60 +0.4871. The plateau is 0.15-0.20 and the shipped value is off it on the generous side by about a factor of two. Two bigs cannot protect the same rim on the same possession, and 47 seasons of shot defence say so.

WHY 0.20 AND NOT 0.15. 0.15 is the peak (+0.5289 against +0.5275) and it is a flat one — the two are inside each other's noise. 0.15 drops the Warriors '17 to an unrounded 75.40 and breaks recal_122's anchor at its floor; 0.20 leaves them at 75.55, which is the only value on the plateau that holds every pin. So 0.20 is the conservative end of an evidence-picked plateau, chosen by a pin rather than by the subject.

FIT, before -> after (mean of the 47 within-season Spearmans of the DEF dial against real DRtg): +0.7764 -> +0.7781. Per decade: 80s +0.8044 -> +0.8044 · 90s +0.8024 -> +0.8057 · 00s +0.8062 -> +0.8091 · 10s +0.7267 -> +0.7270 · 20s +0.7276 -> +0.7300. The round is fit-POSITIVE in four decades and flat in the fifth. This is not a round that spends accuracy to satisfy a ruling; it is a round that found an untested constant sitting off its own evidence, and the ruling is what made anyone look.

WHAT MOVED. 631 of the 1,255 DEF dials, max |move| 2. 0 of the 1,255 OFF dials, and all 1,255 offRaw readings bit-identical — teamOffense is not on this round's path. The pool's mean drtgRef is 110.047736 before and after. The all-time DEF top 15 keeps its six 99s (Celtics '10, Bucks '85, 76ers '80, Bulls '96, Spurs '05 and — newly — Bucks '84 at 98 as the Bulls '98 slip 99 -> 98); the Bulls '98 are the only named five that changed a rank band, and they fall because Luc Longley and Dennis Rodman were the pair the old constant paid twice.

WHY THE SUBJECT ONLY MOVES ONE POINT, stated plainly. Near the summit the DEF gauge runs about 19.9 dial points per raw DRtg point, and 0.181 DRtg per didx point, so a dial point costs 0.28 didx. The subject's anchor loses 0.13 x 0.9 x 0.5 x (117.38 - 105.64) = 0.687 didx from the change, but the POOL mean loses 0.35 of that too and DIDX_HOLD gives it back, so the subject's net loss is 0.34 didx — 1.2 dial points, 96 -> 95. The rim anchor is a 0.117-weighted channel with a ~20-point live range; it cannot pay for four dial points on its own no matter what the constant is set to. Setting ANCHOR_2ND to 0.00 — the second rim protector worth literally nothing, past the truth column's own optimum in the wrong direction — reaches 94 and breaks the Warriors.

WHAT WAS TRIED AND REJECTED, each measured on the whole wheel before being dropped. (a) Flattening recal_122's load profile toward the mean: fit-positive (+0.7832 at flat) but it lowers the Warriors '17 harder than the subject — they are the more top-heavy five — and breaks them at once. (b) Tilting the load profile ONTO the best defender: raises the Warriors, raises the subject too, and costs the subject nothing. (c) ANCHOR_SOFT 0.5 -> 0.2: reaches 94 but the Warriors go to 74.50. (d) Moving the glass or steals weight onto perdef: the subject RISES (they are rich on both). (e) A knee on the glass stack, the same law the anchor got: the subject loses 0.15 didx at best. (f) A top-2 perdef premium, i.e. the literal reading of 'with 2 great': recal_122 already measured and declined it, and re-measuring it here reproduced the same verdict.

HIS SENTENCE, ANSWERED HONESTLY. 'They have 5 good defenders, with 2 great' is exactly right about the roster and it is exactly why the engine reads them high: the five's usage-weighted perdef is 77.60, seventh-best of the 1,255. What the engine was ALSO doing was paying Bobby Jones's rim protection a second time, on top of Moses's, at a rate no season of shot defence supports. That double payment is now gone. What is left — 95, all-time #11 — is the honest reading of a five that really did have Cheeks, Jones, Erving, Barkley and Moses on the floor together, measured as a five and not as a rotation. If he wants the low 90s, the next lever is not on this side of the ledger: it is either the Warriors '17 anchor being re-opened (they are what pins the top-heavy shape in place) or the perdef cards of Erving/Barkley/Moses, which belong to the ratings-to-off-def agent.
